## What the misses say
- **Scale (P1, P2, P5, P10, P11).** I anchored on a starting assumption of "over a million lifetime"
  and on typical monthly volume. Actual 90-day volume is in the table above, and it is
  rising. One requester contract carries most proposals (README, requester split).
- **Resets (P12).** I treated "too early" as a rare edge case. It is the most common
  outcome of a dispute (README, first table). That changes what "overturn rate" means:
  it covers only the minority of disputes that were decided on substance.
- **Rates (P3, P4, P6).** The dispute-rate and overturn ranges held, but the monthly
  overturn rate moved a lot from month to month (`README.md`), so a 30 or 90 day window
  hides that movement.
